member_impact: Dear Member, first the good news: you can still fix this. Your coverage ended on July 6 because the renewal papers went to your old apartment. That is a paperwork problem, not a problem with you. The rules give you a 90-day window to send in your renewal and get your coverage back. If it is approved, your coverage is restored back to July 6, like it never stopped. You do not have to start over with a new application. But the clock is running, so please act this week. Here is what to do: 1) Call a free helper called a navigator, or a legal aid office, right away. They help with exactly this, and it costs nothing. 2) Gather your pay stubs. You work 92 hours a month, which is more than enough. 3) Send your renewal with your pay stubs. You can do it online, by phone, by mail, or in person at the county office. Keep a copy or a confirmation number. 4) Give the state your new address so mail reaches you. Your window runs to about October 4, 2026 — but sooner is much safer. You can do this, and free help is waiting.

citations.quote: If coverage is terminated for a procedural reason — missing paperwork, an unanswered notice — there is a 90-day reconsideration period after the termination date.
Returning the renewal information within it lets the state reopen the case without a brand-new application, and coverage is restored back to the termination date if eligibility is confirmed.
For a passed deadline, a denied exemption, conflicting records, or any notice that does not make sense, a navigator or legal aid should be involved — these are exactly the cases they exist for.
Pay stubs covering the month are the cleanest proof of employment hours.
Demo State (synthetic) accepts reporting online through the member portal, by phone through the state help line, by mail using the form attached to the notice, and in person at a county office.
